subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The 1833 Factory Act introduced significant reform by primarily regulating what?
options: The employment and hours of children in textile mills
questions.explain: The 1833 Factory Act limited the hours of children in textile factories and, crucially, established paid factory inspectors to enforce it.

questions.q: Concern over the poor physical condition of Boer War recruits contributed to the appointment of which 1904 committee?
options: The Inter-Departmental Committee on Physical Deterioration
questions.explain: The 1904 Inter-Departmental Committee on Physical Deterioration investigated national fitness after a high proportion of Boer War recruits were rejected.

questions.q: The Defence of the Realm Act (DORA), giving the government sweeping wartime powers over civilians, was first passed in which year?
questions.explain: DORA was passed in August 1914, allowing the state to control resources, censor news and regulate daily life during the war.

questions.q: The Poor Law Amendment Act, which established the workhouse system and the principle of 'less eligibility', was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The 1834 Poor Law Amendment Act sought to deter pauperism by making relief available chiefly through the deterrent workhouse.

questions.q: During the Crimean War, which nurse became famous for her work at the Scutari hospital from 1854?
questions.explain: Florence Nightingale led nursing reform at Scutari during the Crimean War (1853-56), dramatically reducing hospital death rates.

questions.q: The Haldane Reforms, creating the British Expeditionary Force and the Territorial Force, were enacted between which years?
questions.explain: Richard Haldane reorganised the army between 1906 and 1912, creating the BEF and the Territorial Force ahead of the First World War.

questions.q: In which year was the Great Reform Act passed, redistributing seats and extending the franchise to many middle-class men?
questions.explain: The Great Reform Act of 1832 disenfranchised rotten boroughs and gave the vote to £10 householders, raising the electorate to roughly one in five adult males.

questions.q: Margaret Thatcher became Britain's first female Prime Minister after the general election of which year?
questions.explain: Thatcher led the Conservatives to victory in May 1979, beginning eleven years as Prime Minister.

questions.q: Conscription was first introduced in Britain during the First World War by the Military Service Act of which year?
questions.explain: The Military Service Act of January 1916 introduced compulsory military service for single men, ending Britain's reliance on volunteers.

questions.q: The bitter Miners' Strike against pit closures, led by Arthur Scargill against the Thatcher government, lasted across which years?
questions.explain: The Miners' Strike of 1984-85 ended in defeat for the NUM, a landmark in Thatcher's confrontation with trade union power.

questions.q: The Second Reform Act, which roughly doubled the electorate and enfranchised many urban working-class men, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: Disraeli's Conservative government carried the Second Reform Act in 1867, giving the vote to male householders in the boroughs.

questions.q: The unpopular 'poll tax' (Community Charge), which contributed to Thatcher's fall, was introduced in England and Wales in which year?
questions.explain: The Community Charge came into force in England and Wales in 1990 (a year earlier in Scotland), provoking riots and helping to end Thatcher's premiership.

questions.q: The Falklands War, which boosted Thatcher's popularity, was fought in which year?
questions.explain: Britain recaptured the Falkland Islands from Argentina in 1982 following the Argentine invasion in April.

questions.q: The General Strike, called by the TUC in support of the miners, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The General Strike of May 1926 lasted nine days before the TUC called it off, leaving the miners to struggle on alone.

questions.q: Referendums establishing a Scottish Parliament and a Welsh Assembly, key to Blair's devolution programme, were held in which year?
questions.explain: The devolution referendums took place in September 1997, leading to the first elections to the new bodies in 1999.

questions.q: The disastrous Charge of the Light Brigade took place during which 1854 battle of the Crimean War?
questions.explain: The Charge of the Light Brigade occurred at the Battle of Balaclava in October 1854, immortalised by Tennyson's poem.

questions.q: The wartime coalition that published the influential Beveridge Report identifying the 'five giants' did so in which year?
questions.explain: The Beveridge Report of 1942 attacked Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor and Idleness, laying the blueprint for the post-war welfare state.

questions.q: The 1851 Great Exhibition, showcasing British industrial achievement, was housed in which structure in Hyde Park?
questions.explain: The Great Exhibition of 1851 was held in the Crystal Palace, a vast glass-and-iron structure designed by Joseph Paxton.

questions.q: The Chartist movement presented its third and largest petition to Parliament in which year, amid the Kennington Common gathering?
questions.explain: The third Chartist petition was presented in 1848, the year of European revolutions, following the mass meeting at Kennington Common in London.

questions.q: The People's Charter of 1838 set out six demands. Which of the following was NOT one of them?
questions.explain: The six points were universal male suffrage, secret ballot, no property qualification, payment of MPs, equal constituencies and annual parliaments; votes for women was not included.

questions.q: In which year did women in Britain finally achieve the vote on equal terms with men, at age 21?
questions.explain: The Equal Franchise Act of 1928 lowered the voting age for women to 21, achieving electoral equality with men.

questions.q: Clement Attlee's Labour government won its landslide general election victory in which year?
questions.explain: Labour won the July 1945 general election with a landslide majority, enabling its programme of nationalisation and welfare reform.

questions.q: In which year was the National Health Service founded under Aneurin Bevan?
questions.explain: The NHS came into operation on 5 July 1948, providing healthcare free at the point of use under Bevan as Minister of Health.

questions.q: The 1944 Education Act, which established the tripartite system and free secondary education, is commonly named after which politician?
questions.explain: R. A. Butler's 1944 Education Act ('the Butler Act') created free secondary education with the grammar/secondary modern/technical structure.

questions.q: The Second Boer War, fought between Britain and the Boer republics, lasted between which dates?
questions.explain: The Second Boer War ran from 1899 to 1902, ending with the Treaty of Vereeniging and exposing weaknesses in army recruitment and fitness.

questions.q: The Cardwell Army Reforms, which abolished the purchase of commissions, were introduced in the early 1870s under which Prime Minister?
questions.explain: Edward Cardwell, Secretary of State for War under Gladstone, abolished the purchase of officers' commissions in 1871 as part of wider modernisation.

questions.q: Tony Blair led 'New Labour' to a landslide general election victory, ending 18 years of Conservative rule, in which year?
questions.explain: New Labour won the May 1997 election by a landslide, with Blair becoming Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which Act of 1846 ended protectionist tariffs on imported grain, splitting the Conservative Party?
options: The Reform of the Corn Laws
The Repeal of the Corn Laws
questions.explain: The Repeal of the Corn Laws in 1846, led by Peel, divided the Conservatives and marked a major step toward free trade.

questions.q: The Third Reform Act of 1884 chiefly extended the household franchise to which group?
questions.explain: The 1884 Representation of the People Act extended the borough householder franchise to the counties, enfranchising agricultural and rural workers.

questions.q: The Representation of the People Act of 1918 enfranchised women for the first time, but only those aged over what?
questions.explain: The 1918 Act gave the vote to women over 30 who met a property qualification, alongside near-universal male suffrage.
